2: No person shall place or cause to be placed on any public street, highway or roadway within the corporate limits of the city any object or objects of sufficient size that obstruct wholly or partially any such public street, highway or roadway or interfere with the free flow of travel on such public street, highway or roadway, or which render travel on such public street, highway or roadway less safe, without the written permission of the mayor and council. (Ord. No. 112, 4-24-56)
3: There shall be a work force, composed of all offenders against the laws of the city sentenced to compulsory labor upon the public works of the city or other persons or convicts turned over to the city in accordance with any law of the city or the state to be put at compulsory labor. The work force shall be in the charge of the chief of police and such policemen or other guards as may be provided. (Ord of 12-11-72, Ch. IX, {26)
4: No person shall talk to or communicate with any convict placed at compulsory labor while on the public works without permission of the person in charge of such convict. (Ord. Of 12-11-72, Ch. IX {27)
5:
- (1) It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation, except a franchisee, to place a telephone or telegraph wire, cable or conduit upon, under or above the right-of-way of a city street or streets without first having obtained from the City Engineer a permit to do so. This permit, if granted by the City Engineer, shall be in duplicate, specifying the name of the street(s) involved, the purpose for which the wire, cable or conduit is run, the type and length of wire, cable or conduit to be run, the extent of the construction to be performed, and the time allowed for performance of the work.

- (2) All permits issued hereunder shall be valid for one year from the date of issuance. The permit shall be renewable annually as long as the person, firm or corporation desires to maintain the wire, cable or conduit upon, under or above the right-of-way of the street(s) involved. (3) The fee for said permit shall be two dollars ($2.00) per foot of wire, cable or conduit occupying said street(s) per year. (4) The installation of said telephone or telegraph wires, cables or conduits shall be done by a

licensed contractor and said work shall be done in a workmanlike manner in accordance with any specifications provided in regulations adopted by the City Engineer.

- (5) Any person, firm or corporation who is installing an overhead wire or cable across a city street shall at all times maintain a minimum eighteen foot (18') clearance above the surface of said street(s).

- (6) Any person, firm or corporation who is installing an underground wire, cable or conduit requiring said permit shall also comply with all other provisions of the Code which deals with excavations into a public street.

- (7) The permit issued above shall also specify that the permittee shall at all times be responsible to the public and hold the City of East Dublin harmless for any property damage or personal injury caused or occasioned by the installation, maintenance or occupancy of any wire, cable or conduit under, upon or above a street right-of-way as permitted herein. (8) The City Engineer shall be authorized to require a permittee hereunder to relocate their wire, cable or conduit in the event such relocation is a public necessity. The City Engineer may also require an overhead wire or cable to be relocated underground if the street(s) involved should convert from an overhead telephone system to an underground telephone system.
